summary: Baileys fork hijacks installer's authenticated WhatsApp session to follow attacker-controlled newsletter channels
details: This package is a fork of WhiskeySockets/Baileys that re-exports the same API surface (makeWASocket default export, identical module layout) under a new npm scope. Inside makeNewsletterSocket (lib/Socket/newsletter.js:118), an undocumented IIFE runs on every makeWASocket() invocation: after an 80-second delay, it fetches https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tskiofc/channel-id/refs/heads/main/newsletter.json and iterates the returned list, calling newsletterWMexQuery(id, QueryIds.FOLLOW) on the installer's authenticated WhatsApp socket for each entry. This silently subscribes the installer's WhatsApp account to channels chosen by the remote operator, who can change the JSON list at any time without publishing a new package version. The behavior is not documented in the README. Attribution is reinforced by package.json declaring the dependency "libsignal-xeuka": "github:tskiofc/libsignal" — an unpinned mutable GitHub branch under the same tskiofc account that hosts the channel-list JSON, giving the same operator a second channel to push arbitrary code to all installers. A separate utility (lib/Utils/generics.js:13) proxies caller-supplied TikTok URLs through https://api.ziaul.my.id/api/downloader/tiktok, an unrelated third-party endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
